title: When Similar Means Different: Evaluating LLMs on Arabic--Hebrew Cognates
abstract: arXiv:2606.13218v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Arabic and Hebrew, as closely related Semitic languages, share many words with similar surface forms, including true cognates, false friends, and modern loanwords. These lexical relationships create ambiguity for cross-lingual semantic interpretation, as similar forms may correspond to shared, divergent, or borrowed meanings. To evaluate whether LLMs can make these distinctions, we introduce SemCog Bench, a curated benchmark of 1,858 Arabic--Hebrew word pairs with sentence-level annotations for cognate identification and semantic disambiguation. We evaluate a diverse set of open-source and proprietary LLMs across multiple input representations and contextual settings. Our results show reliance on surface-form similarity, with weaker performance on false friends and wide variation on loanwords. translated_title: 当相似意味着不同：评估大语言模型对阿拉伯语-希伯来语同源词的处理能力
translated_abstract: 阿拉伯语和希伯来语作为密切相关的闪米特语言，拥有许多表面形式相似的词汇，包括真正的同源词、假朋友（形式相似但意义不同的词）以及现代借词。这些词汇关系给跨语言语义解释带来了歧义，因为相似的形式可能对应共同的、分歧的或借用的含义。为了评估大语言模型能否做出这些区分，我们推出了SemCog Bench，这是一个包含1,858个阿拉伯语-希伯来语词对的精选基准，带有句子级标注，用于同源词识别和语义消歧。我们评估了多种开源和专有大语言模型，涵盖多种输入表示和上下文设置。结果表明，模型过度依赖表面形式的相似性，在假朋友上表现较弱，在借词上的表现差异很大。我们进一步发现，上下文和模型规模带来的收益因模型而异，而使用原始文字的输入通常表现最佳。我们的发现揭示了……
tldr: 本文推出了包含1,858个阿拉伯语-希伯来语词对的SemCog Bench基准，评估发现大语言模型在区分同源词、假朋友和借词时过度依赖表面形式相似性，在假朋友识别上表现尤其薄弱。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SemCog Bench, a benchmark of 1,858 Arabic-Hebrew word pairs, revealing that LLMs over-rely on surface-form similarity when distinguishing cognates, false friends, and loanwords, with particularly weak performance on false friends.
